question: What is the main feature of Type III Female Genital Mutilation (FGM)?

options.A: Narrowing of the vaginal opening with a covering seal
options.B: Scraping the walls of the vagina
options.C: Piercing of the outer lips without cutting tissue
options.D: Cutting part of the clitoris only

explanation: Type III FGM, also called infibulation, involves cutting and joining the labia to form a restrictive seal over the vagina. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why does the World Health Organization group FGM into four distinct types?

options.A: To standardise clinical records and research
options.B: To help traditional healers perform it safely
options.C: To calculate the cost of plastic surgery
options.D: To know which types are legal in villages

explanation: Clear categories help healthcare workers communicate properly and track health problems linked to each specific procedure. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which immediate physical complication is most directly linked to severe tissue injury during FGM?

options.B: Heavy bleeding from injured blood vessels
options.C: Weak pelvic floor muscles causing prolapse

explanation: The external female genitalia have a very rich blood supply, so cutting them open often leads to acute and heavy bleeding. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h2)

question: A young girl cannot pass urine and has severe pain right after undergoing FGM. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Complete tearing of the bladder wall
options.C: Swelling and pain blocking urine flow
options.D: Loss of nerve control over the bladder

explanation: Trauma, tissue swelling, and muscle spasms around the urethra make urinating very difficult right after the procedure. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h2)

question: What causes frequent urinary tract infections in women who have undergone infibulation?

options.A: Bacterial infections passed down from birth
options.C: An immune reaction in the bladder
options.D: Blocked or twisted urine flow due to altered anatomy

explanation: The changed anatomy stops urine from draining smoothly, trapping it and helping bacteria to multiply easily. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why do some women suffer from severe menstrual pain years after FGM?

options.A: Increased thickness of the inner womb lining
options.B: Constant womb contractions from nerve damage
options.C: Trapped menstrual blood behind scar tissue

explanation: Scar tissue can block the vaginal opening, stopping smooth menstrual flow and causing painful buildup inside. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is a major reason for a prolonged second stage of labor in women with infibulation?

options.A: Stiff scar tissue blocking the baby's descent
options.B: Early breaking of water drying the pelvis
options.C: Fast opening of the cervix tiring the muscles
options.D: Total lack of womb contractions during labor

explanation: Scar tissue from FGM does not stretch well, acting as a physical barrier against the baby moving down the birth canal. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h4)

question: Prolonged obstructed labor caused by FGM can lead to which serious postpartum condition?
explanation: Constant pressure from the baby's head damages soft tissues against the pelvic bones, forming an abnormal opening between the bladder and vagina. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which psychological condition is often diagnosed in FGM survivors because of their trauma?
explanation: The intense physical and emotional shock of the procedure leaves lasting psychological scars matching post-traumatic stress disorder. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why is painful sexual intercourse a common complaint among women with a history of FGM?

options.B: Relaxed pelvic floor muscles after tissue loss
options.C: Total lack of natural vaginal wetness
options.D: Stiff scar tissue and trapped nerve endings

explanation: Scar tissue lacks natural stretch and can trap sensitive nerve endings, making sexual penetration mechanically difficult and painful. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h5)

question: A nurse is assessing a pregnant woman in Nigeria and suspects a history of FGM. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ignore the topic completely to avoid embarrassing her
options.B: Build trust, ensure privacy, and ask sensitive questions gently
options.C: Carry out a physical check straight away without talking
options.D: Report the patient to security for breaking the law

explanation: Building good rapport and a private, supportive environment helps the patient feel safe sharing her health background. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why should a nurse document FGM findings objectively without showing judgment?

options.A: To keep patient files short and quick to read
options.B: To help the patient get free plastic surgery
options.C: To protect the nurse-patient relationship and ensure good continuity of care
options.D: To gather evidence for prosecuting traditional cutters

explanation: Keeping notes free of judgment maintains trust between the nurse and patient, and helps other health workers provide the right care. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of defibulation surgery for a patient with Type III FGM?

options.A: To relieve blockages and restore normal urine and sexual function
options.B: To remove all remaining nerve endings in the area
options.C: To prepare pelvic tissues for a future closure
options.D: To stop the patient from having monthly periods

explanation: Defibulation cuts open the restrictive scar tissue, relieving urinary blockage, trapped menstrual flow, and painful intercourse. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary role of the nurse in caring for a patient with FGM complications?

options.A: Isolating the patient from family members
options.B: Doing major reconstructive surgeries in the ward
options.D: Coordinating team care and offering compassionate education

explanation: Nurses act as the central link between medical specialists, mental health teams, and the patient while offering supportive guidance. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is a key strategy for nurses working to prevent FGM in local Nigerian communities?

options.A: Working with community and religious leaders to correct myths
options.B: Performing safer versions of the cut in clinics
options.C: Isolating families who practice tradition from getting healthcare
options.D: Relying only on the police without teaching the public

explanation: Working alongside respected community leaders helps shift deep cultural beliefs and encourages communities to stop the practice together. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h8)

question: Why are nurses so important in speaking out against FGM during maternal and child care?

options.A: Nurses are the only ones allowed to treat FGM
options.B: Nurses have direct, trusted contact with families during routine visits
options.C: Nurses can fine families who practice cutting
options.D: Nurses have the political power to pass new laws

explanation: Routine antenatal and child health visits offer the best chance to educate families and protect young girls at risk. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h8)
